entries.prose: This repository is `agent-com`, the RFA (Rooms for Agents) hub and operator CLI.
It is a TypeScript package whose source lives under `src/`.
with CLI commands in `src/cli/commands/`,
TUI components in `src/cli/tui/`,
and eval harness in `src/evals/`.
The package is built with `tsc` (configured by `tsconfig.json`) and publishes two binaries, `rfa` and `agent-com`, both pointing at `dist/cli/main.js`.
Specifications live in `spec/`,
research in `research/`,
and operator-facing templates in `templates/`.
`src/` - hub daemon, engine, CLI, TUI, and eval harness source; the only directory compiled by `tsc`
`src/cli/commands/` - one file per CLI sub-command
`src/cli/tui/` - Ink/React TUI components for the dashboard and onboarding
`src/evals/` - eval runner, gate, judge, label, parity, promote, and trajectory modules
`spec/` - all seven RFA specification documents that govern wire protocol, platform, CLI, concurrency, and egress
`templates/` - files seeded into a new hub directory by `rfa init`, including the eval rubric and case stubs
`test/` - all test files globbed by the `test` script
`scripts/` - standalone runnable scripts for e2e, coldstart, demo, fence-proof, egress-proof, and TUI smoke
`interop/` - the `rfa_min.py` minimal interop artifact
`src/proc.ts` - required spawn helper; child processes must be spawned through this module, never via `npx`
`src/writefence.ts` - keeps `Write`, `Edit`, and `NotebookEdit` out of `allowedTools` for every pack
`src/fenceprobe.ts` - re-proves the fall-through with a live deny probe per guarded built-in at every boot
`src/toolclass.ts` - defines `fenceApplies`, the coverage predicate for the two-door write fence
`src/secrets.ts` - provides `transportToken()`, which resolves the transport credential; clients must call it per request, never capture at import
Build - `npm run build` (runs `tsc`)
Run CLI from checkout - `npm run dev` (runs `tsx src/cli/main.ts`)
Start hub daemon - `npm run start`
Run unit tests - `npm test`
Run e2e scenarios - `npm run e2e`
Run full e2e suite - `npm run e2e:full`
Run evals - `npm run evals`
Run judged evals - `npm run evals:judged`
Run parity gate - `npm run parity`
TUI smoke test - `npm run tui:smoke`
Fence proof - `npm run fence-proof`
Egress proof - `npm run egress-proof`
Cold-start test - `npm run coldstart`
Supervisor - `npm run supervisor`
`RFA_TOKEN` - transport credential read per call by `transportToken()` in `src/secrets.ts`; must appear in a pack's `secrets` declaration
Spawn child processes through `spawnEntry` and `stopTree` in `src/proc.ts`, never `npx`; `spawnEntry` passes tsx's loader by absolute path because `--import tsx` resolves from the working directory

anchor.value: Nothing under `src/` may resolve `agents/`, `data/` or `dogfood/` from the repository root

entries.prose: Resolve the hub directory through `src/hubdir.ts` exclusively; no source file under `src/` may resolve `agents/`, `data/`, or `dogfood/` from the repository root
Find a resident in the process table using `src/procscan.ts`, never a substring match
The fence coverage predicate is `fenceApplies` in `src/toolclass.ts`, never `hasWriteSurface`; a pack declaring `Bash` is fenced for that reason

entries.prose: A check that compares configured against happening must read the running system's own record, not the file the operator edited; honest sources are `state/member.json`, `runs.db`, and the supervisor's state

entries.prose: One knowledge fact must live in exactly one file; check for duplicates before adding a source

entries.prose: Never start anything interactive when stdout or stdin is not a TTY

entries.prose: The `rfa evals parity` gate must be run twice; a single pass has hidden a real regression

anchor.value: After changing `src/`, restart what you are testing

entries.prose: After changing `src/`, restart the affected long-lived process: `rfa agent restart <name>` for a resident, `rfa restart` for the hub and supervisor
The `tsconfig.json` `rootDir` is `src` and `outDir` is `dist`; only files under `src/` are compiled
The `tsconfig.json` target is `ES2022` with `module` set to `Node16`
JSX is compiled with `react-jsx` as set in `tsconfig.json`
Unit tests run with `npm test`, which executes `node --import tsx --test test/*.test.ts test/*.test.tsx`
The `pretest` script enforces Node.js >= 22 before running tests
Test files live in `test/`

entries.prose: A new test file in `test/` is picked up immediately by the glob without any registration step
TUI changes additionally require `npm run tui:smoke`, which drives onboarding and dashboard inside a real pty
Wire scenarios and CLI lifecycle are covered by `npm run e2e`, which writes output to `reports/latest.md`
Deterministic concurrency ordering tests live in `test/interleaving.test.ts`, which drives every ordering with barriers

entries.prose: Stress loops are kept out of `npm test`; nondeterminism belongs in an opt-in soak mode
This repository carries no instance: no `agents/`, `data/`, or `dogfood/` directories (all removed 2026-08-25)

anchor.value: never delete `dist/` without `npm run build` after

entries.prose: Never delete `dist/` without running `npm run build` after, since the linked `rfa` binary executes it
Long-lived processes (hub, supervisor, residents) serve old code after an edit; restart them explicitly after changing `src/`
Run `npm run fence-proof` after every SDK bump; door one of the write fence is version-fragile by design
Run `npm run egress-proof` after every SDK bump alongside `npm run fence-proof`
A bare `allowedTools` entry auto-approves a built-in call before the `canUseTool` callback fires; the SDK emits `CLAUDE_SDK_CAN_USE_TOOL_SHADOWED` when this occurs

anchor.value: a read INSIDE the session cwd is auto-approved and NEVER reaches the callback

entries.prose: A Read built-in inside the session cwd is auto-approved and never reaches the `canUseTool` callback; a Read outside it does reach the callback
`allowUnsandboxedCommands` defaults to true, leaving `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` live; a model used it to escape into the pack tree on the first probe

anchor.value: the SUPERVISOR itself, which is a hub client as well as a process manager: it had no credential and its #ops alerts 401'd silently

entries.prose: The supervisor is a hub client and must resolve its transport credential through `transportToken()`; it had no credential and its alerts 401'd silently
`RfaError` is an exception class carrying a machine-readable `code`, a `message`, an optional `retry_after_s`, and a `data` dict representing an RFA tool-plane error.
`Hub` manages a single MCP endpoint URL and bearer token, exposing a `call` method that retries idempotent tools with bounded jitter and raises `RfaError` on tool-plane or HTTP failures.
`read_result` unwraps one tool result from either SSE-framed or plain JSON, returning the parsed inner object or raising `RfaError` on JSON-RPC or RFA-level errors.
`prune` drops keys whose value is `None` from a dict, because the hub's schemas reject explicit nulls.

`neutralize` strips C0 control characters, bidi overrides, and invisible Unicode from text, and replaces every case variant of `</room-message` with the literal string `</room-message` to prevent frame-breaking.
`strip_tag_block` removes Unicode TAG characters in the range U+E0000–U+E007F from text, which are invisible to a human reviewer but reach a model verbatim.
`attr` allowlists attribute values to alphanumerics and the characters space, underscore, period, hyphen, and colon, producing a string safe for use in XML-style attribute positions without escaping.
`wrap_for_model` renders one peer message envelope as an untrusted-data boundary tag, identical to the hub's own `wrapped` field, so a model never receives raw `body` text directly.
`text_of` extracts raw text from a message envelope for logging and length checks only, and must never be passed to a model.
`Member` manages one room membership: joining, leaving, listening, presence, task work, and message handling, with cursor discipline and epoch tracking.
`headless` runs the CLI in a subprocess with captured output, used by the smoke test to drive non-interactive commands against a target directory.
`free_port` binds a socket on port 0 and returns the OS-assigned port number, then closes the socket.
`smoke` drives both the dashboard and the onboarding scenarios inside real pseudo-terminals against temporary directories, returning 0 on success and 1 with a list of failures otherwise.
`Lane` is the union type `"serve" | "schedule" | "background"` representing the three admission priority classes.
`LANES` is the ordered tuple `["serve", "schedule", "background"]` listing all admission lanes.
`UNSUPERVISED_CAP` is `3`, the fallback concurrency cap used when no supervisor has written a cap to the ledger.
`RATE_LIMIT_PAUSE_FLOOR_MS` is `60_000`, the minimum account-wide hold duration after a provider rate limit.
`VIABLE_BUDGET_USD` is `0.05`, the minimum remaining budget below which admission is refused rather than starting a turn that would be truncated.
`BudgetRequest` carries the optional per-day and per-task USD ceilings, the spend day string, and the viability floor used at admission time.
`spendDay` formats a `Date` as a `YYYY-MM-DD` string representing the budget day, defaulting to the current date.
`Lease` describes one row in `account_leases`, including the lease id, agent, lane, run id, pid, timestamps, park state, reservation amount, spend day, and row kind (`"lease"` or `"maintenance"`).
`Admission` is the result of an `acquire` call: an `ok` flag, the granted `Lease` or null, a refusal `reason`, optional `detail` and `retry_after_s`, and the `granted_usd` ceiling passed to the SDK.
`Settlement` records the attribution of one completed lease: agent, lane, run id, spend day, granted ceiling, actual cost, and timestamps.
`RateLimitReport` is one row from `account_rate_limits`, carrying the agent, run id, detail string, timestamp, and auto-increment id.
`AccountSnapshot` describes the current ledger state: cap, in-flight and parked counts, per-lane and per-agent breakdowns, pause state, all live leases, and active maintenance markers.
`isRateLimitError` returns `true` when an error's message matches patterns for HTTP 429, rate-limit, too-many-requests, usage-limit, or quota-exceeded responses.
`AUTH_FAILURE_MARKERS` is the canonical list of LIKE-syntax patterns used to identify credential failures, shared between the resident's refusal logic and the observability alert.
`isAuthError` returns `true` when an error's message matches any pattern in `AUTH_FAILURE_MARKERS`, indicating a bad or expired credential rather than a transient failure.
`pidAlive` sends signal 0 to a pid and returns `true` if the process exists or is owned by another user (`EPERM`), and `false` for non-positive or non-integer pids.

`AccountLedger` manages the SQLite-backed admission table, providing `acquire`, `release`, `park`, `unpark`, `settle`, `sweep`, `setCap`, `cap`, `pause`, `beginMaintenance`, and snapshot methods over `account_leases` and related tables.
`ACTION_IDENTITY_EXT` is the wire extension key `"io.github.pbeneteau/action-identity"` used to carry a stable action identity on approval cards.
`EFFECT_CLASS_EXT` is the wire extension key `"io.github.pbeneteau/effect-class"` used to carry the effect class of an action on approval cards.
`EffectClass` is the union type `"irreversible" | "reversible_with_cost" | "reversible"` classifying how an action fails when its outcome is unknown.
`EFFECT_CLASSES` is the tuple `["irreversible", "reversible_with_cost", "reversible"]` listing all valid effect classes.
`DEFAULT_EFFECT_CLASS` is `"irreversible"`, the safe default applied when an effect class is absent or unrecognised.
`effectClassOf` returns the `EffectClass` for a raw value, falling back to `DEFAULT_EFFECT_CLASS` for any unknown or absent input.
`mayRetryUnsettled` returns `true` when an unsettled claim on the given `EffectClass` may be taken over and re-run, which is false only for `"irreversible"`.

`normalizeInput` recursively normalises a tool input value for identity purposes: NFC-trimming strings, dropping absent-ish values from objects, stripping identity-blind keys, and preserving array order.
`actionIdentity` computes a stable `act1_`-prefixed SHA-256 identity for an action from its tool name, normalised input, and scope, stable across retries and process restarts.
`actionScope` returns a scope string for an action derived from its task id, conversation id, or room, in that priority order.
`InterruptRule` describes one matched interrupt rule, carrying the tool name pattern and the interrupt behaviour.
`interruptMatch` returns the first `InterruptRule` from a pack's `interrupt_on` list whose pattern matches `toolName`, or `null` if none match.
`ApprovalOutcome` carries the result of a human approval wait: the verdict, the decliner's identity if declined, and whether the deadline expired.
`DEFAULT_APPROVAL_WINDOW_MS` is `30 * 60_000` (30 minutes), the fallback approval window when no reply deadline is available.
`approvalWindowMs` derives the approval window from the asker's `reply_by` deadline, clamped so the card never outlives its audience.
`refusalForOutcome` maps an `ApprovalOutcome` to the wire refusal reason `"deadline_expired"` or `"declined"`, or `null` when the action was approved.
`humanAction` returns a human-readable label for a tool name, used in approval card descriptions.
`previewLines` formats a tool input record as a short multi-line preview string for display in an approval card.
`requestApproval` sends an approval card to the room via the sidekick member and waits for a human verdict, returning an `ApprovalOutcome`.
`joinSidekick` joins a hub room as the resident's sidekick observer member and returns the resulting `RoomMember`.
`GeneratedArtifactRecord` describes one generated artifact: its path, content hash, and the run that produced it.
`ArtifactsFile` is the shape of the `artifacts.json` store, holding an array of `GeneratedArtifactRecord` entries.
`artifactsStore` returns a `JsonStore<ArtifactsFile>` backed by `<hub>/runtime/artifacts.json`.
`recordGeneratedArtifacts` appends or updates artifact records in the hub's `artifacts.json` store for a completed run.
`ArtifactDrift` describes a generated artifact whose on-disk content no longer matches the hash recorded at generation time.
`artifactDrift` compares a list of `GeneratedArtifactRecord` entries against live file hashes and returns the subset that have drifted.
`CANDIDATE_SELECTORS` is the tuple `["human", "first-verified"]` listing the valid candidate selection strategies.
`CandidateSelector` is the union type of the values in `CANDIDATE_SELECTORS`.
`isCandidateSelector` is a type guard returning `true` when a value is a valid `CandidateSelector`.
`SELECTOR_NOTES` maps each `CandidateSelector` to a human-readable description string.
`CandidatePlan` describes a resolved fan-out plan: the number of candidates, the selector, and the per-task budget.
`planCandidates` validates and resolves a candidate fan-out request into a `CandidatePlan`, enforcing that `concurrency >= candidates`.
`StartedCandidate` carries the run id and task reference for one candidate turn that has been dispatched.
`CandidateProduct` holds the output of one completed candidate run: its answer text and cost.
`CandidateOutcome` pairs a `StartedCandidate` with its `CandidateProduct` or failure reason.
`CandidateSetResult` is the result of a full fan-out: all outcomes, the selected winner index, and the selector used.
`RunCandidateSetOpts` carries the inputs to `runCandidateSet`: the plan, the task, the agent context, and selection callbacks.
`runCandidateSet` runs N candidate turns in parallel for one task, applies the selector, and returns a `CandidateSetResult` with all outcomes and the winning candidate.
`roomsBlock` generates the YAML `rooms:` block for an agent.md frontmatter given a room name and binding options.
`knowledgeBlock` generates the YAML `knowledge:` block for an agent.md frontmatter from a list of glob patterns.
`setTopBlock` rewrites a named top-level YAML block in agent.md text, replacing it with the provided block string.
`setRoomsBlock` rewrites the `rooms:` block in agent.md text using `setTopBlock`.
`bindPack` rewrites the `rooms:` block in a pack's agent.md file on disk, validated before the write, and returns the updated definition.
`addKnowledge` appends or merges glob patterns into the `knowledge:` block of a pack's agent.md file on disk.
`setTopScalar` rewrites a named top-level scalar key in agent.md text, with options to insert it if absent.
`dropNestedKey` removes a named key from a named top-level YAML block in agent.md text.
`MODE_LINE` is a function returning the `mode: <mode>` YAML line string for a given `AgentMode`.
`setAgentMode` rewrites the `mode:` scalar in a pack's agent.md file on disk to one of `ask`, `plan`, or `bypass`.
`yamlScalar` returns a YAML-safe scalar string, quoting the value when necessary.
`PackChanges` carries the set of optional fields that `editPack` may update: description, model, per-day budget, offer, concurrency, and candidates.
`EditResult` carries the outcome of an `editPack` call: the updated text, the parsed definition, and a list of human-readable change descriptions.
`currentSettings` extracts the current description, model, and other editable settings from an `AgentDef` for use as defaults in an edit flow.
`editPack` applies a `PackChanges` to agent.md text, validates the result, and returns an `EditResult` with the updated text and change list.
`CHAIN_EXT` is the wire extension key `"io.github.pbeneteau/chain"` carrying the hash-linked chain reference on room events.
`COUNTER_ASK_EXT` is the wire extension key `"io.github.pbeneteau/pending-counter-ask"` annotating a 2-cycle counter-ask advisory.
`CHAIN_DEPTH_CAP` is `8`, the maximum chain hop depth at which the chain extension stops propagating rather than the request being refused.
`ChainRef` carries the chain id, depth, and parent hash for one hop in a request chain.
`readChain` extracts a `ChainRef` from an extension bag, returning `null` if absent or malformed.
`mintChainId` generates a new random chain id string.
`nextChain` advances a `ChainRef` by one hop, returning `null` when the depth cap is reached.
`BlockedChains` tracks in-flight chain ids to detect deadlock cycles, exposing `add`, `remove`, and `wouldDeadlock` methods.
`wouldDeadlockDetail` returns a human-readable string describing the deadlock a given `ChainRef` would create.
`genesisFor` returns the genesis hash string for a room's event chain, derived from the room handle.
`hashedForm` returns a copy of an event record with its hash field populated, used when appending to the chain.
`linkOf` extracts the chain link object from an event record.
`ChainDivergence` describes a point where the event chain fails verification, naming the seq and the expected versus actual hash.
`ChainResult` carries the outcome of `verifyChain`: a `valid` flag and any `ChainDivergence` found.
`verifyChain` walks an array of event records and returns a `ChainResult` indicating whether the hash chain is intact from genesis.
`CHAIN_SCOPE_QUALIFIER` is the fixed string appended to chain verification output explaining what the chain proves and does not prove about hub-side edits.
`MEMORY_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS` is the tuple `["mcp__memory__delete", "mcp__memory__rename", "mcp__memory__str_replace"]` naming the memory tools restricted to the consolidation lane.
`agentDefSchema` is the Zod schema that validates a parsed agent.md frontmatter object into an `AgentDef`.
`CONCURRENCY_GATE_LABELS` is the array of human-readable labels for each concurrency gate check.
`concurrencyGateFailures` returns the list of gate failure messages for a definition that does not satisfy all concurrency preconditions.
`writeSurfaceDefFailures` returns validation failure messages for a pack's declared write surface.
`resolvePackCwd` resolves a pack's declared `cwd` relative to its pack directory, returning the absolute path.
`reachAcknowledgementFailure` returns a failure message when a pack's reach declaration is missing required acknowledgement fields, or `null` when valid.
`fencedCwdFailure` returns a failure message when a fenced pack's declared `cwd` is outside the permitted root, or `null` when valid.
`AgentDef` is the TypeScript type inferred from `agentDefSchema`, representing a fully parsed and validated agent pack definition.
`declaredSecretNames` returns the union of secret names declared by a pack's own `secrets` field and by its MCP servers.
`AgentPack` carries a loaded pack's directory path, parsed `AgentDef`, and raw agent.md content.
`splitAgentMd` splits agent.md content into its YAML frontmatter string and body string.
`parseAgentMd` parses agent.md content into a validated `AgentDef`, throwing on schema violations.
`loadPack` reads and parses the agent.md in a pack directory, returning an `AgentPack`.
`listPacks` returns all valid `AgentPack` entries found under an `agents/` root directory.
`BrokenPack` carries the name and parse error for a pack directory whose agent.md could not be validated.
`scanPacks` returns both valid `AgentPack` entries and `BrokenPack` entries found under an `agents/` root.
`packByName` looks up a single pack by name under an `agents/` root, throwing if not found or broken.
`declaredPackNames` returns the sorted union of names from valid packs, broken packs, and an existing name list, used to detect collisions before a write.
`deriveCard` builds an `AgentCard` from a loaded `AgentPack`, used when joining a room.
`knowledgeFiles` returns the list of file paths matched by a pack's knowledge glob patterns.
`Attachment` describes one knowledge source attachment: its local path, remote URL, and sync state.
`AttachError` is thrown by `attachKnowledge` when a knowledge source cannot be attached, carrying a human-readable reason.
`attachKnowledge` clones or links a knowledge source into a pack's directory and updates the pack's agent.md knowledge block.
`agentNew` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa agent new`, which creates a new agent pack interactively or headlessly.
`agentLs` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa agent ls`, which lists all packs in the hub directory.
`agentShow` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa agent show`, which prints the parsed definition of a named pack.
`agentValidate` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa agent validate`, which validates a pack's agent.md and reports errors.
`agentBind` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa agent bind`, which rewrites a pack's room binding in its agent.md.
`supervisorCommand` sends a start, stop, or restart command for a named agent to the running supervisor and returns a status string.
`agentStart` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa agent start`, which starts a named agent via the supervisor.
`agentStop` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa agent stop`, which stops a named agent via the supervisor.
`agentRestart` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa agent restart`, which restarts a named agent via the supervisor.
`EditOutcome` extends `EditResult` with the applied pack name and whether the agent was restarted after the edit.
`applyPackEdit` validates and writes a `PackChanges` to a pack's agent.md, optionally restarting the agent, and returns an `EditOutcome`.
`editInEditor` opens a pack's agent.md in the operator's `$EDITOR` and returns the exit code.
`changesFromFlags` builds a `PackChanges` object from CLI flag values, returning `null` when no flags produced a change.
`agentEdit` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa agent edit`, which edits a pack's settings interactively or headlessly.
`agentReflect` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa agent reflect`, which distills a pack's judged eval record into lessons.
`agentMode` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa agent mode`, which sets a pack's operating mode to `ask`, `plan`, or `bypass`.
`agentRetire` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa agent retire`, which removes a pack from the hub directory.
`completionScript` returns the shell completion script string for the given shell type.
`complete` returns completion candidates for the given word list against the router's command tree.
`completionCommands` returns the `CommandDef` array for the `completion` subcommand group.
`clientHubUrl` returns the hub URL a CLI client should connect to, derived from the hub directory's configuration.
`writeProjectSkill` writes the MCP skill configuration for a room into a Claude or Cursor project directory and returns the list of files written.
`connectClaude` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa connect claude`, which writes the MCP configuration for Claude Desktop.
`connectCursor` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa connect cursor`, which prints the MCP configuration for Cursor.
`connectMcp` is the `CommandDef` for `rfa connect mcp`, which prints the generic MCP configuration block.
The CLI entry point is `src/cli/main.ts`, which installs as the `rfa` and `agent-com` binaries from `dist/cli/main.js`.
The hub process (`src/main.ts`) serves HTTP and persists state in a SQLite store under the hub directory's `.rfa/data/` path, using `better-sqlite3`.
External services are reached through the Anthropic Claude Agent SDK and the MCP client and server packages declared in `package.json`.
`src/` - core runtime: hub, engine, dispatch, sessions, store, credentials, signing, egress, and all agent lifecycle modules
`src/cli/` - operator CLI: routing, prompts, scaffolding, and command implementations that front every hub operation
`src/cli/commands/` - individual CLI command modules (agent, connect, creds, dash, doctor, init, ops, room, server, talk, and others)
`src/cli/tui/` - Ink/React terminal UI components including the dashboard, onboarding wizard, agent editor, and palette
`src/evals/` - evaluation pipeline: runner, judge, gate, parity, label, promote, trajectory, and concurrent eval modules
`src/servers/` - MCP server integrations (Linear)
`src/hub.ts` - hub HTTP server
`src/engine.ts` - agent run engine
`src/dispatch.ts` - task dispatch
`src/supervisor.ts` - process supervisor for resident agents
`src/writefence.ts` - two-door write fence keeping `Write`, `Edit`, and `NotebookEdit` out of `allowedTools` for every pack
`src/fenceprobe.ts` - live deny probe run at every boot to re-prove write-fence fall-through per guarded built-in
`src/egress.ts` - egress and declared surface enforcement
`src/toolclass.ts` - tool classification including the `fenceApplies` coverage predicate
`src/hubdir.ts` - the single module that resolves paths onto the hub directory
`src/proc.ts` - child-process spawning via `spawnEntry` and `stopTree`, used instead of `npx`
`src/procscan.ts` - process-table scanning to locate residents without substring matching
`src/secrets.ts` - transport credential resolution via `transportToken()`
`src/signing.ts` - log signing
`src/logverify.ts` - log verification
`src/knowledge.ts` and `src/knowledge-sources.ts` - knowledge source tracking and sync
`src/mcplaunch.ts` - spawns MCP servers of the `command` and `builtin` forms through srt, one instance each per server's own sandbox block
`src/mcpsandbox.ts` - MCP sandbox configuration
`src/memoryfs.ts` - memory filesystem
`src/consolidate.ts` - memory consolidation
`src/candidates.ts` - candidate fan-out for parallel task runs
`src/turnlock.ts` - turn lock enforcing the serial-loop invariant
`src/account.ts` - account and budget ledger
`src/obs.ts` - observability
`src/bridge.ts` - room bridge
`src/posture.ts` - exposure posture
`src/principals.ts` - principal identity
`src/credentials.ts` - credential management
`src/migrate.ts` - hub directory migration
`interop/rfa_min.py` - minimal Python interop reference implementation
`scripts/` - operator scripts: e2e, coldstart, demo-push, fence-proof, egress-proof, watchdog-replay, tui-drive, repair-obs-cost
`spec/` - RFA specification documents (versions 0.1 through 0.9)
`templates/` - files seeded into new hub directories by `rfa init`, including the eval rubric, service definitions, and skill templates
`console/` - web console static assets
An operator request enters through `src/cli/main.ts`, which routes to a command in `src/cli/commands/` or the TUI in `src/cli/tui/`.
Commands that need hub state open the store via `src/hubdir.ts` when no hub is running, or call the hub's HTTP API when one is.

A task dispatched through `src/dispatch.ts` is picked up by `src/engine.ts`, which launches a resident agent process via `src/proc.ts` and `src/mcplaunch.ts`; the resident's writes pass through the two-door fence in `src/writefence.ts` and `src/fenceprobe.ts` before reaching `src/memoryfs.ts` or the run scratch surface.
Observability events flow through `src/obs.ts`, and the completed run's episode is available to the eval pipeline in `src/evals/runner.ts`.
Transport credential resolution is centralised in `transportToken()` in `src/secrets.ts`; callers read `RFA_TOKEN` per call, never at import time
Child-process lifecycle is managed through `spawnEntry` and `stopTree` in `src/proc.ts` to ensure SIGKILL propagates to the process group
Write-fence enforcement is applied at startup by `src/writefence.ts`, which keeps `Write`, `Edit`, and `NotebookEdit` out of `allowedTools` for every pack
Boot-time fence probing is performed by `src/fenceprobe.ts`; `bypassed` and `inconclusive` results are both fatal
Tool surface classification uses `fenceApplies` in `src/toolclass.ts` to determine whether the write fence applies (any built-in of class `guarded` or `command`)
Log integrity is provided by `src/signing.ts` (signing) and `src/logverify.ts` (verification)
Observability is collected in `src/obs.ts`
Error types are centralised in `src/errors.ts`
Background knowledge sync takes a drain barrier in the account lease table before pulling, coordinated through `src/account.ts`
The eval reliability gate is run with `npm run evals`
The parity gate is run with `npm run parity`
The write-fence proof is run with `npm run fence-proof`
The egress proof is run with `npm run egress-proof`
`templates/service/launchd.plist` - launchd service definition for macOS deployment
`templates/service/systemd.service` - systemd service definition for Linux deployment
The `build` script compiles TypeScript sources from `src/` to `dist/` via `tsc`
The `engines` field in `package.json` requires Node.js `>=22`
The `pretest` script enforces Node.js major version 22 or above before running tests
The `coldstart` script (`npm run coldstart`) packs, installs into a fresh prefix, and answers one question to validate end-to-end packaging
Lane types use string union literals declared as `export type Lane = "serve" | "schedule" | "background"`
Constants that are re-exported from another module keep their original name, e.g. `EFFECTIVE_DEFAULT_CAP` re-exported from `src/hubdir.ts` via `src/account.ts`
Extension wire keys follow reverse-domain notation, e.g. `"io.github.pbeneteau/action-identity"` assigned to `ACTION_IDENTITY_EXT`
Boolean predicate functions are prefixed with `is`, e.g. `isRateLimitError` and `isAuthError` in `src/account.ts`
Admission result interfaces use noun phrases, e.g. `Admission`, `Lease`, `Settlement`, `BudgetRequest` in `src/account.ts`
Effect class values are lowercase kebab string literals: `"irreversible"`, `"reversible_with_cost"`, `"reversible"` collected in `EFFECT_CLASSES`
Private class fields use the `private` keyword rather than `#` syntax, e.g. `private db: Database.Database` in `AccountLedger`
Duration constants are suffixed `_MS` for milliseconds, e.g. `LEASE_TTL_MS`, `UNPARK_GRACE_MS`, `RATE_LIMIT_PAUSE_FLOOR_MS`
The identity prefix encodes the normalization version as a string literal `"act1_"` prepended to the hex digest in `actionIdentity`
Core runtime modules live directly under `src/`
CLI entry point and command modules live under `src/cli/`
CLI subcommands are individual files under `src/cli/commands/`
TUI components are TypeScript/TSX files under `src/cli/tui/`
Eval pipeline modules live under `src/evals/`
MCP server integrations live under `src/servers/`
All test files live under `test/` and are named `*.test.ts` or `*.test.tsx`
Operator scripts (e2e, coldstart, proofs) live under `scripts/`
Wire and platform specifications live under `spec/`
Seed templates for hub directory initialization live under `templates/`
The interoperability reference client lives at `interop/rfa_min.py`
Node built-ins are imported with the `node:` protocol prefix, e.g. `import Database from "better-sqlite3"` alongside `import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto"`
The project uses ES module syntax (`"type": "module"` in `package.json`) with `.js` extensions on local imports in compiled output, e.g. `from "../src/proc.js"`
Internal modules are imported by relative path with `.js` extension as required by Node16 module resolution, e.g. `from "../src/egress.js"` in `scripts/egress-proof.ts`
`tsconfig.json` sets `"moduleResolution": "node16"` and `"module": "Node16"`, enforcing explicit extensions on relative imports
The `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` client is imported from its scoped subpath, e.g. `from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js"`
JSX is compiled with `"jsx": "react-jsx"` in `tsconfig.json`, used by TUI components under `src/cli/tui/`
Domain errors are typed classes extending `Error`, e.g. `RfaError` in `interop/rfa_min.py` carries `code`, `message`, `retry_after_s` and `data` fields
`HubDirError` is caught by name and its `.hint` field is printed before `process.exit(2)`, e.g. in `scripts/repair-obs-cost.ts`
Admission refusals are typed via the `reason` discriminant on the `Admission` interface: `"account_paused"`, `"cap_reached"`, `"budget_exhausted"`, `"maintenance"`

Auth failures are detected by `isAuthError` using a shared `AUTH_FAILURE_RE` regex derived from `AUTH_FAILURE_MARKERS`, so the resident and the observability alert cannot classify the same error differently
Rate-limit detection is centralised in `isRateLimitError` in `src/account.ts` and matched by `RATE_LIMIT_RE`
Mutating RPC calls in `interop/rfa_min.py` are not retried blindly; only idempotent reads listed in `IDEMPOTENT` are retried with bounded jitter
Process exit codes are explicit: `process.exit(1)` for operational failure, `process.exit(2)` for bad arguments or missing hub directory
The test runner is Node's built-in `--test` flag, invoked as `node --import tsx --test test/*.test.ts test/*.test.tsx`
A `pretest` script guards the minimum Node version before any test file loads
End-to-end scenarios are in `scripts/e2e.ts` and run via `npm run e2e` or `npm run e2e:full`
Live fence behaviour is proved by `scripts/fence-proof.ts`, run via `npm run fence-proof`
Live egress behaviour is proved by `scripts/egress-proof.ts`, run via `npm run egress-proof`
TUI smoke tests are driven by `scripts/tui-drive.py` via `npm run tui:smoke`
The eval reliability gate runs via `npm run evals` or `npm run evals:judged`
Concurrency interleaving tests live in `test/interleaving.test.ts` and use barriers rather than timing
The write-fence deterministic half lives in `test/writefence.test.ts`
Hub directory path-resolution is regression-tested in `test/hubdir.test.ts`

entries.prose: Rate-limit events are recorded to `account_rate_limits` with `agent`, `run_id`, `detail`, `at` and `handled` columns
Auth failure markers are defined as `AUTH_FAILURE_MARKERS` in `src/account.ts` in SQL LIKE syntax and compiled into `AUTH_FAILURE_RE` for runtime use
The `AccountSnapshot` interface exposes `in_flight`, `parked`, `by_lane`, `by_agent`, `paused_until`, `pause_reason`, `leases` and `maintenance` for operator inspection
Script language is inconsistent: operator scripts are TypeScript (`scripts/e2e.ts`, `scripts/fence-proof.ts`) except the TUI driver which is Python (`scripts/tui-drive.py`)

Retry logic style differs between layers: `interop/rfa_min.py` uses an explicit `RETRY_DELAYS_S` list with bounded jitter, while `src/account.ts` uses a `UNPARK_GRACE_MS` polling approach with no shared retry abstraction

**Room protocol** - agents join rooms, discover members by capability digest, and exchange messages over MCP using tools including `room_create`, `room_join`, `room_send`, `room_listen`, `room_roster`, `room_task`, `room_admin`, and `room_watch`
**Operator CLI (`rfa`)** - the front door for onboarding, the dashboard, agent lifecycle, room management, credentials, evals, and log verification
**Agent packs and supervisor** - local agents are defined as packs and managed by `src/supervisor.ts`
**Two-door write fence** - implemented in `src/writefence.ts`, keeping `Write`, `Edit`, and `NotebookEdit` out of `allowedTools` for every pack
**Egress control** - the declared surface proved live by `npm run egress-proof`
**Evals and parity gate** - reliability gate run via `npm run evals` and `npm run parity`
**TUI dashboard** - implemented in `src/cli/tui/dashboard.tsx`
**Room console** - a live web view served by the hub, located at `console/index.html`
**Interop reference client** - `interop/rfa_min.py` is a dependency-free Python reference client for non-RFA agents
**Service templates** - `templates/service/launchd.plist` and `templates/service/systemd.service` for running the hub under launchd or systemd
**OTel observability** - one span per tool call via `src/obs.ts`, joining the caller's trace when `_meta` carries a `traceparent`
Node.js `>=22` is required, as declared in the `engines` field of `package.json`
The package name is `agent-com` and the installed binary is `rfa`, as declared in the `bin` field of `package.json`
Install from the repository with `npm install -g git+ssh://git@github.com/pbeneteau/agent-com.git`
Run `npm install` to install dependencies after cloning
The `pretest` script checks that Node.js major version is at least 22 before running tests, because the `better-sqlite3` binding requires Node 24 in some environments
TypeScript sources compile to `dist/` via `npm run build` (invokes `tsc`)
Run the CLI from this checkout with `npm run dev -- --help`
Start the hub process with `npm run start` (invokes `tsx src/main.ts`)
Start the supervisor with `npm run supervisor` (invokes `tsx src/supervisor.ts`)
Run the spec's worked example in memory with `npm run demo`
Run the push demo with `npm run demo:push`
Run evals with `npm run evals` (equivalent to `tsx src/cli/main.ts evals run`)
Run judged evals with `npm run evals:judged` (equivalent to `tsx src/cli/main.ts evals run --judged`)
Run the parity gate with `npm run parity` (equivalent to `tsx src/cli/main.ts evals parity`)
Run the TUI smoke test with `npm run tui:smoke` (invokes `python3 scripts/tui-drive.py --smoke`)
Prove the write fence with `npm run fence-proof` (invokes `tsx scripts/fence-proof.ts`)
Prove egress with `npm run egress-proof` (invokes `tsx scripts/egress-proof.ts`)
Run the coldstart check with `npm run coldstart` (invokes `tsx scripts/coldstart.ts`; needs a model credential)
The CLI entry point is `src/cli/main.ts`; the hub entry point is `src/main.ts`
`RFA_TOKEN` - the transport credential read per call by `transportToken()` in `src/secrets.ts`
`RFA_HUMAN_KEYS` - environment form for human principal keys
`RFA_MCP_TOKENS` - environment form for MCP transport bearers
`RFA_PUSH_URL` - environment form for the push notification URL
`RFA_CONSOLE_URL` - environment form for the console URL

`policies/gate.json` is the pre-delivery policy gate; the template ships at `templates/gate.json`
`src/env.ts` is the module that handles environment variable access
Run the unit and integration test suite with `npm test` (globs `test/*.test.ts` and `test/*.test.tsx`)
Run end-to-end scenarios with `npm run e2e` (invokes `tsx scripts/e2e.ts`; writes `reports/latest.md` and `latest.json`)
Run the full e2e suite with `npm run e2e:full` (invokes `tsx scripts/e2e.ts --full`)
Run the TUI smoke test with `npm run tui:smoke` for changes under `src/cli/tui/`
Build TypeScript sources with `npm run build` (invokes `tsc`; output goes to `dist/`)
The TypeScript compiler targets `ES2022` with `module` set to `Node16`
JSX is compiled with `react-jsx` transform, as set in `tsconfig.json`
`npm run fence-proof` and `npm run egress-proof` are run after every SDK bump; they require a real OS sandbox and a real model
The deterministic concurrency test lives in `test/interleaving.test.ts`

A systemd service template is provided at `templates/service/systemd.service`
The published package includes `dist`, `console`, `templates`, `interop`, `INTEROP.md`, `spec`, `README.md`, and `LICENSE`, as declared in the `files` field of `package.json`
